_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#6 — PREDICT: TangDis buys Newton iterations, not convergence, and the size of the saving is the part the entry had to be corrected on. Four arms on a four-element geometrically nonlinear SOLID HEX8 cantilever (YOUNG 1000, NUE 0.3, tip surface Neumann ramped over ten steps, TOLDISP 1e-10 / TOLRES 1e-09), two load levels x two predictors, run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. The RESULT DESCRIPTION is pinned to the SAME tip dispy for both predictors at each load and passes in all four runs (RESULT_FAILURES_*=0, all exit 0), so the predictor changes only the path to equilibrium and never the equilibrium. The cost: ConstDis spends exactly ONE more Newton iteration than TangDis at every one of the ten steps, at both loads (PER_STEP_PENALTY=[1] in both cases, 62 total against 52) — CONSTDIS_COSTS_EXACTLY_ONE_MORE_PER_STEP=yes and CONSTDIS_IS_AN_ORDER_SLOWER=no. That is a 20% surcharge, which is why TangDis is worth setting to trim iterations and is not a remedy for a diverging solve. The ratio marker is computed from Newton iteration counts (nlniter), never from elapsed time; it was originally named ..._IS_AN_ORDER_SLOWER, which claimed a timing result this fixture does not measure and tripped the wall-clock gate on the word alone. Renamed to say what it computes.

_mutation.note: remove the contrast: give the ConstDis arm at load 100 the tangent predictor. Its iteration count drops to TangDis's, the per-step penalty set becomes [0] and TOTAL_ITERS_CONST_100=62 disappears, so the fixture must go red.
same at load 600. TOTAL_ITERS_CONST_600=62 disappears and PER_STEP_PENALTY_600 flips to [0], so the fixture must go red.
